title: Baquet, Bechet, Johnny Dodds and reading at the Villa
summary: Baquet played straight; Bechet clean in style; Dodds tied keys down; reading music at the Villa.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: How would George Bacquet play? Would he play sort of a straight, or would he play all little-

Oh no, he played straight, you know. Looks like he played straight to my remembering, you know, because there's so much changes, you know, been made for different musicians there. That's why I'm trying to figure out how did Bé Ché play, you know, during the time he used to come in. Well, I was going to ask you, how did Sidney play?

Well, he played equally wonderful, and I liked his style, you know, that's what I say. He played some kind of, but he used to cut in, you know, so much, that funny stuff, but he was clean, you know, with it, you know. A fella can be clean with his style, you know.
He'd come and sit right into the band when you were playing too, huh?

Now, this fella, Johnny Dott, he was a good clanness player too, isn't he? But, he had his credit tied down, all the keys tied down, mostly. And I picked up his answer one night, he used to have, on 3rd Street, you can call that place, something they used to call that place. But anyhow, he used to turn it over, I think, at that time.
What do you mean, tied down, had rubber bands or something?

Yeah, rubber bands, yeah. And I couldn't make that sharp, you know. He didn't use any keys. No, no, no. He didn't make those sharp supplies. No, no, no, no. And I, I've been used to making that, you know. And when I got to make them, the key was tied down, but I couldn't do nothing.
He just played it in an edge, a little key. Yeah, he got your key, that's all. That's all. Well, he'd play everything in an edge. Oh, man.
How did Sidney, what kind of an instrument did Sidney Bechet have then? Do you remember anything about his hand?
I believe he was about to send me.
Yeah. Them guys had it, you know. I had to give it to him, you see. That's why I said, I was glad I got with somebody that could read, you see. That's where I was. He kept me out the storm.
The pastor put up the music and then Sidney couldn't plan to go on home.

And Joe Howard himself, you know, he couldn't memorize much. He had to read, you know. He read everything. Yeah, everything, see. That's why I got by by letting by air, you see. Well, you think fellas just learn, just have to read, well, they won't make, they won't go too far in what they might hear, you see. Yes. Just like me, after I got on those climate, well, I couldn't remember songs like I did when I first started, you see. Because playing that side harmony, you know, you get away from that lead, you see. But I could remember, if I heard your song, I could go in and play it right now. But since I got on the climate, and now I'm on base, you see, well, I don't pay much attention to songs now, you see.
